free_tier.stated: No documented per-snippet storage cap; snippets are git-backed and unlimited in count, but contribute to namespace storage accounting
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free, Cloudflare-fronted like all of GitLab.com; snippets are cloneable and downloadable via API.

tooling: Snippets API (POST /snippets), git clone of the snippet repo, glab CLI, VS Code extension. Rate limited to 300 creates/hour/authenticated user.
chaining: Snippets are versioned git repos -> unlimited snippets x unlimited versions. The 300/hour creation limit is the only throttle, which is trivially high for a bulk loader. Storage counts toward namespace storage but is NOT enforced.
limits_note: 300 creations/hour/user, shared with the GraphQL createSnippet mutation. No documented file or snippet size cap found on the snippet docs page. Worth treating as 'unbounded but undocumented' rather than verified bulk capacity.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Snippets are visible/searchable by other users when public; storage is accounted at namespace level so it is the most likely subject to be capped first if GitLab ever enforces namespace quotas.
